newsitem.title: FRANCE: Canal Plus in film rights deal with Universal.
newsitem.headline: Canal Plus in film rights deal with Universal.

text.p: French pay television broadcaster Canal Plus on Monday signed an exclusive long-term film rights deal with Universal Pictures, securing an important source of movies for the digital television age.
Canal Plus officials declined to give financial details.

The French broadcaster started its Canalsatellite digital satellite television service on April 27. A rival French consortium, TPS, is due to start services before Christmas and recently signed up the Paramount and MGM Hollywood studios for around $650 million.

In a statement, Canal Plus and the MCA subsidiary of Canada's Seagram group said they reached a long-term agreement, including exclusive film rights and the creation of a special Universal channel on Canalsatellite. Universal Pictures is part of MCA.
Canal Plus and Germany's Kirch Gruppe both claim to have Europe's biggest catalogue of film titles.

The Universal channel "will be dedicated to action-adventure/mystery product drawing upon French and European programming as well as Universal's extensive library of titles from this genre, such as "Columbo", "Magnum P.I.", "Murder She Wrote" and "The A-team", Canal Plus said.
The deal also gives exclusive pay television rights to Canal Plus and Canalsatellite for recently released movies "Waterworld", "Babe" and "Apollo 13", as well as Universal's library of older films.

"This agreement solidifies the 10-year association that Universal has enjoyed with Canal Plus and we are delighted to have this opportunity to build and broaden this mutually beneficial relationship," Blair Westlake, president of Universal Pay Television and Television Business Development, said.

Pierre Lescure, chairman of Canal Plus, said: "This agreement...also marks a new area of cooperation between Europe's leading pay TV network and a U.S. major studio. It symbolises a common strategic approach -- together we are entering the digital age."

The rival TPS -- Television Par Satellite -- consortium is headed by commercial broadcaster TF1, itself owned by Bouygues and state-owned France Television. Lyonnaise des Eaux unit M6 and Compagnie Luxembourgeoise de Telediffusion (CLT) are also part of the grouping.
CLT operates the RTL channels in Germany and the Benelux countries and a small eastern part of France.
